title: The Concept of Social Capital in Modern Communities
text:
Social capital refers to the network of relationships among individuals, enabling them to achieve mutual benefits. It involves factors such as trust, shared norms, and reciprocal obligations within a community. High levels of social capital are often correlated with stronger economic outcomes and better public health metrics.

Sociological theory distinguishes between various types of social capital, including bonding (ties among homogeneous groups) and bridging (ties that connect diverse groups). While bonding capital provides strong support within an in-group, overly reliance on it can sometimes lead to insularity or polarization. Conversely, bridging capital is crucial for accessing broader resources and opportunities outside the immediate circle.
